title: Rank surfaced lessons by anchor specificity
description:
query_for_context sorts only by `verified DESC, confidence DESC` (src/lessons.rs:434). A lesson anchored to a single symbol is far more relevant to the current context than one anchored to a whole directory, but they compete equally for the cap slots.

This is where most of the token-efficiency win lives, independent of which tool does the surfacing — a tighter cap is only safe if the top slots are reliably the most relevant lessons.

acceptance_criteria.text: Symbol-anchored lesson outranks directory-anchored lesson at equal verified/confidence
Specificity derived from the anchors that actually matched, not all anchors on the lesson
Cap can be lowered without losing the most relevant lesson in test fixtures

decisions.decision: Split file anchors across two specificity tiers instead of one, giving literal file paths rank 3 (above import_pattern) and glob file anchors rank 1 (below it).
decisions.rationale: The plan's flat order (symbol > import_pattern > file > directory) treats 'src/lessons.rs' and 'src/**/*.rs' identically, but the first binds to exactly one file and the second can match a whole tree — broader than an import pattern. Checking for glob metachars is a one-line discriminator.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Flat four-tier order as specified in the plan: simpler, but systematically under-ranks the most precise anchor kind the store supports.

implementation_plan: query_for_context already tracks matched_anchors (which anchor keys caused each lesson to surface). Derive a specificity score from the narrowest matching anchor kind: symbol > import_pattern > file > directory. Sort by (verified, specificity, confidence). Feeds directly into being able to lower CONTEXT_SURFACING_CAP.
execution_record: Specificity rides on SurfacedLesson as a #[serde(skip)] u8 rather than staying local to query_for_context, because orient (sutra/277) merges per-file result sets and re-sorts them — without the field on the struct that merge would silently drop the ranking. Both new tests were verified to fail against the pre-change code (stashed src, ran suite) before being accepted as regression tests.
